evidence: src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: reserve() adds up quantities per productId and checks product.availableStock < quantity before changing any product. This is a business invariant, so it belongs in the domain.
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: it throws DomainError for a missing product or insufficient stock. These are domain errors.

src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: it depends only on the ProductRepository port injected through the constructor and declared in src/domain/repositories.ts. There is no concrete persistence, HTTP or framework code.
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: product.reserve(quantity) and product.release(quantity) hand the state changes to the Product aggregate.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: StockReservationService is a domain service. It enforces business invariants: it adds up the requested quantity per product, checks that each product exists and has enough stock before changing anything (all-or-nothing reservation), and calls the Product aggregate's own reserve/release behaviour. Its only persistence contact is the ProductRepository port, which is declared in the domain (src/domain/repositories.ts). The file has no storage, transport or framework code. Calling repository.save from a domain service is a recognised DDD pattern and is not infrastructure logic. The doc comment mentions an 'in-memory catalogue', but that is wording in a comment, not a responsibility the code carries. No ADR prose is given that would conflict. Every responsibility fits the domain layer.
